intro.fallback: Most people at {{ account.name }} could answer these from memory. This puts the answers on one page.

fallback.title: Write down the ten decisions your team makes most
fallback.body: Ten decisions, one page each. New hires ramp faster, and you see which steps a system could take over.

fallback.title: Agree on five Monday numbers and one view that holds them
fallback.body: Choose the five figures every manager reads on Monday, build the single view that shows them, and retire the spreadsheets that fed the old ones.

fallback.title: Put the three most repeated handoffs on rules
fallback.body: Pick the three handoffs your team repeats most each day and let software do them before you add people. It is usually where the first month of time comes back.

fallback.title: Name one owner for improvement, with two hours a week
fallback.body: One person, a backlog, and a slot every week. It is the cheapest change on this page and it makes the other moves stick.

recipe.prompt:
You are writing copy for an operations maturity self-assessment page for {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}). {{ sender.name | default: 'The sender' }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} sends it. The page asks eight questions across four areas (Process, Data, Automation, Team), scores the answers from 1 to 4, and shows where {{ account.name }} stands next to its peers. "We" and "us" mean {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }}.

Inputs: account.industry, account.size_band, account.dossier.summary and account.dossier.why_now describe {{ account.name }}. The reader is {{ person.first_name | default: 'not named' }}, {{ person.title | default: 'title not known' }}. Nothing else. You do not know how mature {{ account.name }} is: the reader has not answered yet.

Return JSON with these keys:
- headline: 20 to 90 characters, a question about {{ account.name }}'s operations, in sentence case. "How mature are {{ account.name }}'s operations?" is the plain version; change it only if the dossier gives a more specific word than operations.
- intro: 1 or 2 sentences, 40 to 220 characters, spoken to the reader, on why a few minutes on this is worth it for a {{ account.industry }} company of {{ account.size_band }} people. Start with the reader's first name only if it is given. Draw on the industry, the size or the dossier; add no fact about {{ account.name }} that those inputs do not state. Say nothing about how mature they are. Do not write "pick the closest option" or anything about honesty: the page adds that line after yours.
- steps: exactly 4 items, in this order: Process, Data, Automation, Team. Each is {title, body}. The page shows the three that match the reader's weakest areas, so each one has to stand alone. title is at most 70 characters, one concrete move that starts with a verb. body is 2 or 3 short sentences, 40 to 320 characters: what to do first, and what it gives a {{ account.industry }} company of {{ account.size_band }} people. This is common practice for companies like that, not a claim about {{ account.name }}.

Facts: use only the inputs. Never invent customers, numbers, tools, results or quotes about {{ account.name }} or anyone else, and never add a statistic.

Voice: one person talking to a peer. Plain, specific, a little warm. Short sentences a person would say out loud.

Rules for every string: no em dashes or en dashes. No exclamation marks. No email addresses or phone numbers. No hype words (unlock, leverage, seamless, robust, crucial, elevate, delve, transform, game changer, cutting-edge, best-in-class). Never "real" as emphasis.

recipe.rubric:
Grade the page copy the way its reader meets it: the headline, then the intro, then the four steps. 10 is copy a busy operations lead reads once and finds specific to their company.
Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- specific: the intro and the steps fit the account's industry and size from the inputs, and could not be pasted onto any other company unchanged.
- plain: short sentences, plain words, one idea per line, no jargon stack.
- honest: no claim about {{ account.name }}'s current state, no flattery, no invented number, customer, tool or result.
- usable: each step is one move a team could start this week, and the four steps do not repeat each other.
Automatic fail: an em dash or en dash, an exclamation mark, an email address or phone number, a hype word, or any sentence that says how mature {{ account.name }} already is.
